newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to slip on crude, unsold supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to slip on crude, unsold supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were assessed lower as weak fundamentals and overnight losses in crude forced prices to edge lower, traders said.
December Brent on the IPE dropped a hefty 88 cents a barrel in London on Thursday, placing bearish sentiment, traders said.
An offer was seen for 180-cst cargo for loading in November at $117, a dollar lower from Thursday. Bids/offers were at $117/$119 on Thursday.

Traders said ample supplies would also place pressure on prices. They said a Kuwaiti cargo remained on offer. Seller was heard offering the cargo at $1 per tonne over Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
Traders considered the offer too high and said it should hover between 50 and 75 cents per tonne.
Thailand's cargo for November loading from Rayong was already sold but price details were not immediately available, traders said.
South Korean cargoes for November loading were still seeking homes, a trader said.
Traders said there were more offers than bids in the market in recent weeks, indicating a weak market.
They stocks were also high in Singapore.
Chinese demand remained slack but Indian tender to buy 25,000 tonne for delivery November 15-18 may help absorb some lengths in an oversupplied market, traders said.
In the swaps market, November paper was discussed at $115.50/$116.50, lower from Thursday quotes at $117.25/$117.75.
